premises: Local chemical ordering (LCO) can form in initially random solid solution HEAs under thermal activation
LCO regions act as barriers that pin dislocations and increase lattice friction (e.g., Peierls stress)
Increased lattice friction inhibits plastic flow, reducing toughness and promoting brittle fracture
High strain-rate loading combined with modest thermal activation triggers LCO formation
The proposed mechanism operates under specific service conditions (high strain rate, moderate temperature)
